A Perfect Blend of Nostalgia and Modern Innovation. A Perfect Blend of Nostalgia and Modern Innovation

I've been using the Motorola Razr+ 2023 for a few weeks now, and it has been an outstanding experience. As a long-time admirer of the original Razr, I was thrilled to see how Motorola has beautifully reimagined this iconic design with cutting-edge technology.

Design and Build Quality

The design of the Razr+ 2023 in Infinite Black is truly striking. It feels luxurious in hand, and the folding mechanism is both smooth and sturdy. The external display is not only convenient for quick glances at notifications but also enhances the overall aesthetic appeal of the phone.

Display

The 6.7-inch P-OLED main display is vibrant and offers excellent clarity and color accuracy. Watching videos and playing games on this screen has been a delightful experience. The 2.7-inch G-OLED external display is equally impressive, providing a quick and easy way to interact with the phone without unfolding it.

Performance

Equipped with the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 processor and 8GB of RAM, the Razr+ 2023 handles multitasking and high-performance apps seamlessly. I experienced no lag, and everything from launching apps to switching between tasks was smooth. The 256GB of storage is more than sufficient for my needs, accommodating apps, photos, and videos comfortably.

Camera

The camera system is versatile and produces high-quality images. The 50MP main camera captures detailed and vivid photos, even in low light. The 13MP ultra-wide camera is great for capturing expansive shots and group photos. The front-facing camera, combined with the external display, makes taking selfies very convenient.

Battery Life

The battery life is impressive. The 3500mAh battery easily lasts me through a day of heavy usage, including streaming videos, browsing, and gaming. The fast charging feature is a huge plus, allowing me to quickly recharge and get back to using the phone without much downtime.

Software and Features

Running on Android 13, the Razr+ 2023 provides a clean and user-friendly interface. Motorola's subtle enhancements improve the experience without overwhelming the user with unnecessary features. I particularly appreciate the Ready For platform, which allows seamless connectivity with other devices.

Overall Experience
The Motorola Razr+ 2023 in Infinite Black is a fantastic device that combines the nostalgic charm of the original Razr with modern smartphone capabilities. Its stylish design, excellent performance, versatile camera system, and impressive battery life make it a standout choice for anyone looking to upgrade their smartphone. I highly recommend it for those who appreciate both form and function in a mobile device.

Refined design and amazing cameras!. I first want to talk about the design and I’m simply nuts over it. I have the black version (obsidian) and it’s a stunner with super clean lines throughout. The dark grey accents around the edges that blend into the camera bump are also a nice blend of just enough gloss without looking chrome. 

The front glass blends right into the rest of the case with a subtle, curved edge where the display spills over the edge just slightly. 

The 120Hz display is also fantastic and can get extremely bright. Combine that with the large size and its fantastic for watching videos and reading eBooks is also a great experience.

It also has a combination of both a fingerprint unlock hidden in the display as well as face unlock and this is something that I wish all phones have (looking at you, iPhone). Having the option of using my finger if, let’s say I’m wearing sunglasses that prevent my face from being recognized, or vice versa, using face unlock if I’m wearing gloves, is just super handy.

Google Pixel phones have been hailed as having amazing cameras and photo quality and this new Pixel 7 Pro continues that trend with 3 versatile cameras on the back as well as a quite capable front-facing camera.

The main camera shoots 50, yes 50 megapixel images, and combine that with the f1.85 lens, you can get high quality images from your phone that are actually perfectly appropriate to make larger sized prints.

The 7 Pro also has a 12 megapixel ultra wide lens and it also has a 48 megapixel telephoto camera and gotta say, compared to many other zoom lenses on other flagship phones, the image quality is simply stellar.

Battery life is fantastic for me where I’m easily getting through a full day of use and I tend to be on my phone a lot.

Another reason I like this phone a lot is the flexibility you have with both a physical SIM tray as well as an eSIM. This makes the 7 Pro a really good option if you travel and want to pop in a SIM card from a different country.

Sound quality is one area where I wasn’t as impressed where the sound was OK but just wasn’t quite as full as I would expect out of this size of phone. The volume also seems to be slightly less compared to other phones but that may actually be a good thing because at the loudest setting, the sound can get tinny. 

Overall, I’m super impressed with the 7 Pro with very few shortcomings I can think of. For the price, this is hands-down the flagship phone to choose if you want an Android phone.

First impressions. I just got the Pixel 7 on Friday the day after the release day. I'm migrating from a Samsung S21 5G so I've always gravitated towards the value, smaller flagship phones. Trade-in amount was great direct and almost covered the full cost of the phone/equal to what I paid for it. It was mainly for the great intro deal that I jumped at upgrading a phone that was only 1.5 years old. Also read about the Samsung batteries expanding...

Nondescript package came 1 day after ordering. In box, comes with USB-C cable and a USB to USB-C adaptor, no AC adaptor plug at all. I had thought about getting the lemongrass then the white but ended up getting the boring black on the advice of my daughter but also thought it would stand up to wear and tear the best. Out of the box it's very very glossy. It's OK but it's had fingerprints since you first touch it. One weird thing is the box was scuffed up on the outside and the phone had particles on it like it had been opened but this was straight from the factory.

I tried to use an eSIM to activate and save the trip to the store but a las the technology didn't work and phone got stuck in a activation no where land. Luckily on Saturday there was a store open that could help me out b/c the phone support is closed on weekends?! Long story short, store was able to get on the phone with their "specialists" and get the phone activated by using a physical SIM.

After that, brought the phone home went through the menus and use a USB-C to migrate my apps, data over in no time. Easiest upgrade ever (aside from the activation hiccup which is par for course). Overall first impressions is it's a much nicer phone that my Samsung Galaxy S21. Feels better built with more weight with a cleaner more responsive UI than the Samsung One UI. I looked at online videos to learn how to switch between active apps.  I really never did like or find value in all the Samsung apps, much prefer a pure, clean OS which of course the Pixel is.

Power button, volume up/down are flipped between the Samsung and the Pixel but intuitively I much prefer the Pixel with the power on the top. As I said, I mainly got the Pixel b/c of the trade-in deal that essentially made the phone free to upgrade. I saw the launch event and was very excited about the unblur photo option and being a tech person all the AI/ML stuff enabled by the new Tensor G2. So far after 2 days very glad I upgraded.

I have to confess I also upgraded b/c I was having issues with cellular connectivity on through my Verizon MVNO carrier and I read online that this could be a Samsung issue. I'm not a gamer and use my phone mainly to text, as a MFA code generator, for vendor apps (restaurants, transit), and web browsing so my demands are not that great. I'll report back after a while with an update on reliability and any issues found.

I've been using the Samsung Galaxy A16 for a while now, and overall, it's a solid phone—especially for its price point. But there are definitely some things I like and a couple I don't.

What I Like:

Battery Life: This phone lasts all day with no problem. I can use it for social media, music, videos, and texting without needing to constantly recharge.

Display: The screen is clear and bright, and it's a good size for watching videos or browsing.

Performance: It handles everyday apps smoothly—no major lag, even with multiple apps running.

Camera: Pretty decent in good lighting. Photos come out clear and colorful, and it has some fun editing features built in.


What I Don't Like:

No Headphone Jack: One of the biggest downsides for me. I really miss having a regular audio jack. Not everyone uses Bluetooth earbuds, and I feel like this was a step back.

Low-light Camera: The camera struggles in darker settings, which is common for budget phones.

Storage: You'll probably need a memory card if you take a lot of pics or download big apps.

Speaker: It works fine but isn't super loud or high quality—better with headphones or a speaker.


Overall:
The Samsung Galaxy A16 is a great budget phone for everyday use. It's reliable, has a good battery, and looks nice. But if you're someone who still likes using wired headphones, the lack of a headphone jack might be frustrating. Still, for the price, it holds up well.

I've been an iPhone user for a long time, so I never considered an Android phone. The Google Pixel 9 feels nice in hand, but it's a bit slippery and I've dropped it a few times, causing some scratches on the screen. It's lightweight and easy to handle and has a 6.3-inch screen, which is a good size.

There are 4 colors available, and I think they all look great, especially the Peony version.

The camera is probably my favorite thing about this phone. The photo and video quality is stunning, and I love the various editing options. The "add me" feature is great for group photos, allowing you to add yourself into the shot. The Magic Editor is perfect for content creators, and the Audio Magic Eraser is fantastic for reducing background noise in busy places like restaurants or concerts. These features are all built into the camera app, so there's no need to download extra apps.

Gemini is another great tool on this phone that makes life easier. It responds to specific requests, helps find and respond to emails, and can open apps for you. There's a paid version called Gemini Advance, which costs $20 a month and offers more capabilities. It's not essential, but I decided to try it since it comes with a free month. I don't usually use these types of apps, but I thought I'd give it a try.

The Pixel Screenshot feature organizes all your screenshots, making it easy to search for them using keywords.

The phone's screen is incredible, with vibrant colors and clarity. I use my phone for watching videos, movies, and social media, and the audio quality is loud and clear.

Overall, this is an amazing phone and definitely worth the price. If you're a content creator who needs a great camera and editing options on the go, I highly recommend it.

Design & Display
The design is sleek, with a matte finish that feels premium in the hand, and the 6.5-inch Full HD+ display offers vibrant colors and sharp details. It’s a smooth and immersive experience, whether I’m watching videos, playing games, or scrolling through social media. The 120Hz refresh rate is a nice touch for fluid navigation and responsiveness.

Performance
Powered by a solid MediaTek Dimensity chipset and 6GB of RAM, the Moto G 5G handles multitasking and day-to-day tasks with ease. Apps open quickly, and even gaming sessions are smooth, thanks to the reliable performance. Plus, the inclusion of 5G support ensures that you can take advantage of faster data speeds when available, making this a future-proof choice for the price.

Camera
The 50MP main camera is a standout for the price range. Daylight shots are crisp and vibrant, and the macro lens adds versatility to the photo experience. The 13MP front camera delivers great selfies with plenty of detail, even in lower lighting conditions.

Battery Life
Battery life is excellent. With a 5000mAh battery, I easily get through a full day of use, even with heavy screen time. Plus, the 20W fast charging means you don’t have to wait long to get back to 100%.

Software & Features
Motorola has kept the software clean and close to stock Android, with a few helpful Moto features like gesture controls and a custom Moto app. It’s a pleasant, bloatware-free experience. Plus, the 5G connectivity is a huge plus for anyone looking to stay ahead of the curve.

Final Verdict
The Moto G 5G 2024 is an excellent value for the price. It combines a great display, solid performance, and a capable camera in a well-built device. If you're looking for a budget-friendly smartphone with 5G capabilities, this is definitely a top contender.

No regrets!. I switched from my old Samsung to this iPhone out of curiosity, and I wholly do not regret it.

First of all, the Touch ID works incredibly well and instantaneously. Simply resting your thumb or finger on the Home button (which isn’t a button at all, but works satisfyingly well) unlocks your phone right away with hardly any delay. I’ve already experienced this feature on my iPad, but having it on my phone is so much better because I use it for so much more. Because of it, I can get to my messages, phone, music, etc. much faster than having to put in my PIN every time.

The display is bright and colorful as well. The resolution is technically low, but it looks crystal-clear when you hold it in your hand. Everything from movies to photos look nice on the display.

Speaking of photos, the camera on this iPhone is not bad at all. It might not be as good or have as many features as the cameras on more expensive models like the iPhone 12, but if you’re not interested in those fancy features, the camera on the iPhone SE will work for you. And it’s still better than my old Samsung, so it’s a complete upgrade for me.

The connection I get between my iPhone and other Apple devices is jaw-dropping. When I use a pair of AirPods Pro, it instantly connects the moment I put them into my ear. I can see my photos and messages from my phone on my iPad as well. And though I plug in my iPhone to my PC for iTunes, I still get that sense of hassle-free connectivity. The feeling of uniformity and seamless connection is great and works wonders.

All in all, if you have been wanting to switch to an iPhone or want to try it for the first time, this is a great place to start. It’s also a great deal too!

Samsung Galaxy A16: A Strong Display Undercut by Frustrating Issues
​The Samsung Galaxy A16 offers a genuinely impressive multimedia experience for its price point, largely thanks to its vibrant display and capable camera. However, a couple of significant usability issues keep it from being a truly flawless budget contender. The biggest highlight is undoubtedly the visual quality. The screen is bright, clear, and makes watching videos or browsing photos a pleasure. Similarly, the picture quality from the camera is excellent, capturing details and colors that are far better than what you might expect from a phone in this category. Where the A16 stumbles is in two key areas. The first is a clear omission in design: the lack of a standard 3.5mm earphone plug-in. This forces users who prefer wired headphones, or who rely on them in their car or other devices, to purchase a separate USB-C adapter or switch entirely to Bluetooth earbuds. It's an unnecessary inconvenience that subtracts from the phone's overall value. The second, and more critical issue, is the recurring error when trying to place a call. A phone that struggles with its primary function—making calls—is deeply frustrating. Whether this is a software bug, a network compatibility problem, or a hardware glitch, this unreliability must be addressed to make the phone dependable for daily use. Conclusion: The Samsung Galaxy A16 is a good, feature-rich phone that nails the basics of viewing and photography.

It’s not a pro by name, but it acts like one. If you’re looking to save a few dollars and not interested in the pro features found on the…well, pro models, then the baseline pixel 9 is not going to disappoint. There are really not too many mega features added to the pro models that the average user will miss. Of course, if you’re typically a user of the more advanced features, you’ll want to jump up to the pro level, but the basic everyday user will be more than happy with the 9. Actually, I was surprised to see just how many new and old features were included in the base model and really was only bummed to find the “pro” setting in the camera was missing. But given the name, it makes sense why it is exclusive to the pro models. Still, other phone makers will include the pro settings in all levels and I am kinda confused why google would pull it. The ability to change shutter speed and manual focus etc is not all that “pro” despite the mode name, and as a photographer, I really prefer to have manual controls as an option. And while on the subject of the camera, I personally also don’t like all the auto post editing being done to my photos to “enhance” them, but I know I’m going to be in the minority here and most people will welcome the auto adjustments being made. This includes things like color adjustments, lighting and sharpening. To be fair, it usually does make the image look better, but I would prefer to have an option to leave my shots untouched. (and maybe I haven’t found that toggle yet.) 
  That said, the camera is very good, it has the same lenses as the pro model minus the tele lens. I don’t know why phone makers are doing this, but the idea that we all would rather have a wide angle lens vs a tele zoom lens as our second lens is confusing to me. The wide angles are usually useless and have such bad distortion on the edges that the images are usually useless. I do find myself wanting to zoom in on something far away much more often. But the 2x digital zoom is at least better quality than other phone makers attempts at this. Again, if you feel the need for another lens, buy the pro model. If you’re just a casual shooter, this will work just fine. 

Design: 
  The new look of the pixel 9 is mostly welcomed. The gorilla glass 2 front AND back is a nice addition. Protecting your device from scratches and cracks better. But I don’t really like the feel/weight of the device. It’s top heavy from the giant camera bulge that makes holding the phone a little awkward at first. After a few days I got used to it more, but it’s still noticeably heavier and top heavy. I also don’t like the apple style straight sides. They make holding the phone feel a little less comfortable than rounded edges and the desire to look more like an iPhone always makes me unhappy. If I want an apple product, I’d buy it. I like android because it’s NOT apple. But that’s personal preference obviously, the part that matters is it’s also just more uncomfortable in the hand. This is all not super important though if you plan on getting a case on the device. Which I would recommend because the camera bump makes laying the phone on it’s back a little awkward, but laying it on it’s face without a case will risk scratching the front screen without a case to provide a little lift. The bezels are flush without a case. That said, I haven’t put a case on it yet, and other than being a little too slippery for my pockets (the phone would fall out of short pockets in the car and couch often) it’s not so slippery or awkward that I’m desperately trying to get a case on it. 

Battery: 
  The battery is a little bigger than the pixel 8 but having come from a samsung device and not an older pixel, I’m not sure about the comparison to older models. What I do know is there is little to no chance you will run out of battery before the end of day. Even with massive screen use, camera use, voice calls etc, I was still able to make a full day on a charge. Which is a good thing because charging is still insanely slow compared to other phone designs. 30 minutes gets you about 50% charge and a full charge takes over an hour. Unless you wireless charge, which will then take….well too long to clock. I haven’t actually checked because I never had time to waste. What I do know is my car charger is wireless and while running google maps for driving and the screen on, it pretty much held the battery steady but didn’t charge very fast. Over a couple hour drive it went up maybe 10 percent. This will vary based on chargers and use obviously but the idea of getting a quick top up while driving doesn’t sound possible unless you plug it in. Again, not a big deal though because I’m still not running into low battery issues. I also love the adaptive charge option which will slow charge overnight so it’s full by the time your alarm goes off. I had an alarm for 9am and woke up early at 8 and it was full charged. I was asleep so I don’t know how long it took, but in theory it should help long term battery life. 

Last Thoughts:  
  There are a few other things worth mentioning, although I’m not sure they are all exclusive to the pixel 9. Among all of the new AI features we’re seeing in basically everything with a network connection now, there are a few handy features. I love the ability to screen calls, something that was perfect timing as I have recently had my number sold or hacked because I get about 15 spam calls a day. Now the auto screening is taking care of that for me. However, googles support site says that pixel 7 and above has the option to manually choose which calls to screen, but I do not have that option as of now. I also was told by google that there is an option to make a private partition where you can have applications and files etc behind a password or lock pattern/fingerprint. I have not been able to find this feature yet either but seems similar to samsungs “secure folder” and I assume it’s somewhere, I just haven’t found it yet. This MAY also just be a feature coming in the next android version. Which brings me to the next point, with the release coming earlier than normal, the pixel 9 has the same android version as the others but will of course get the latest update when it comes out. And that is going to be the theme for 7 years, with google saying they will cover 7 years of updates so assuming your battery, screen, or apps don’t get outdated, you can use this phone for a long time. 
  The pixel also comes with gemini, but I have not been impressed YET and still prefer google assistant but I think as time goes on, gemini will be a much better AI assistant. I don’t love that you have to pay for a “premium” version, and will not be doing that, but if you don’t mind throwing more money at google, it will not be a regrettable purchase. 
 Lastly, the new feature to have satellite supported SOS is really nice piece of mind. Although, I don’t usually go places without cell coverage, it does seem most of the time that I am out of range is when I am most likely to need help. Things like snowboarding on the backside of a mountain or hiking deep in the woods. It’s nice to know you can still get help if you need it. 
 Rounding out the new stuff is a load of camera AI features and editing help that you can find info on alllll over the internet, so I won’t get into that now, but suffice it to say, there's plenty of stuff to do to scratch your creativity itch. 

OVERALL I am enjoying the pixel 9 as a daily driver and although I’ve always been partial to the samsung phones, I think Pixel has really stepped up their game and made a device worth getting over others. Despite a few buggy issues with apps and battery charging woes or the occasional awkward drop on my face, I still think the pixel 9 brings a lot of amazing features and sleek new look to the pixel family. The fingerprint sensor works well from the start and learns as it goes, getting even more accurate along the way, the inclusion of new AI features and all the tools provided by google make this device a pro level phone without the pro name.

Great phone. Pros: The Flip 5 has great battery life (better than the Flip 4 or the Galaxy S22)! The external screen is very useful for checking texts, the weather, calendar, etc, without opening the phone. (MAJOR upgrade from the Flip 4.) Get a phone case with a screen protector for the external screen, though...probably a good idea to keep this phone in a seperate pocket than your keys or change!  The phone easily fits into just about any pocket and the indentation where the screen folds is noticeably shallower than the previous model. The usb-c port was also upgraded on this year's model and can be used (with an adapter) to output upto 4K video to a monitor/tv. The 5G, Wifi6e, apps and processing are all seem just as quick and reliable as other high-end smart phones. Cons: the cameras are basically the same as the Flip4 and are pretty mediocre.  Low light/night photos from the main cameras and especially, the selfie camera, are pretty dim.  (The cameras on my old Galaxy S10 took better pictures, especially at night.)  The hinge where the phone bends was supposedly upgraded from the Flip4, but it doesn't seem to hold the phone open as strongly as the pervious model...it require less force to open/close, though that may have been intended as a feature? (I find myself accidently partially closing my screen if I move the phone too quickly in certain directions.)  The external screen doesn't support full apps, only widget versions of some apps. There seems to be a bit of lag when taking some photos, but not others, not terrible, but noticeable compared to the Flip4 or Galaxy S22. When trying to access photos saved in the "Gallery"  from Facebook or Chrome browser, there's a strange 1~3 second lag before your camera roll will display, which is irritating...that DIDN'T happen on the Flip4. Remains to be seen: The Flip3s and Flip4s had an issue with the factory-installed screen protector eventually bubbling-up and seperating from the screen at the bend after about 1 year of use...hopefully Samsung has corrected that issue. Overall, a great phone, but due to its few short-comings, best to buy this phone when it's on sale.

The Perfect Bang for you Buck Smart Phone. I recently upgraded to the Google Pixel 8 with 128GB of storage, and I am really impressed with the smartphone experience Google offers. From its design to performance and camera capabilities, the Pixel 8 has exceeded my expectations in every way, making it one of the best smartphones I’ve owned.

The Pixel 8's design is sleek with a modern look. Its slim profile and premium materials not only make it aesthetically pleasing but also very comfortable to hold. Where some smartphones have almost gotten too big. The Pixel 8 in my opinion, is the ideal size phone and fits perfectly in all my pants pockets. The attention to detail is there, and the phone feels incredibly well-built. The placement of buttons and fingerprint sensor is intuitive, in that they are easy to reach and enhances the overall user experience.

The 6.2” OLED display on the Pixel 8 is stunning. The 1080x2400 resolution makes the colors vibrant, and the sharpness is on point. Whether it's watching videos, scrolling social media, or playing games, the display makes everything pop. The 120Hz high refresh rate ensures smooth scrolling and pinpoint responsiveness, making every interaction with the phone feel seamless. The display itself comes equipped with Gorilla Glass 7 which is one of the most durable glass screens on the market, and because of this I don't feel the need to put a screen protector on it compared to other phones on the market. (That being said I will still be putting a case on the phone, to protect the corners and the back glass). 

The Pixel 8 is equipped with Google’s powerful Tensor G3 processor and paired with 8GB of RAM, which allows the Pixel 8 to deliver lightning-fast performance. This makes multitasking a breeze, where I can pull up a youtube video, leave the app and it will still be playing in a popup video player while in a different app on the screen. This phone handles everything I throw at it with ease, providing a snappy and responsive user experience. The Pixel 8 runs on Android 14, and the experience is fluid and for the most part bloatware-free , with some random google owned apps like Fitbit. The integration of Google services is seamless, and the phone receives timely updates and security patches. The addition of new features, such as gestures, face unlock and other customization options enhances the overall usability, making the phone a joy to use. An under the radar addition to the Pixel 8 phone is the new Wi-Fi 7 chip allowing for even faster wireless speeds when connected to Wi-Fi. At the moment of writing this, there are not many affordable Wi-Fi 7 routers available to the average consumer. That being said, the addition of Wi-Fi 7, is great foresight for future proofing the phone as Wi-Fi 7 becomes more affordable, allowing the customer to be able to get the fastest speeds. At home I’m currently using a Wi-Fi 6e router and was able to get speeds over 600 Mbps, which is the fastest I’ve personally been able to get over my 6G network on a wireless device. 
Google has promised up to 7 years of software support for the Pixel 8, giving you peace of mind knowing that your phone will not slowly be phased out or slowed down as newer phones come out which is huge. One thing that can not be understated enough is the integration of other Google software and apps. If you have a gmail email and use any of the other Google services, the integration of those is seamless, just by simply logging in with your gmail account and all of your workbooks and spreadsheets from your google docs and sheets are there on your phone. Security nowadays is more important than ever with people’s data and information getting stolen everyday and with the Pixel 8, Google has added their own VPN (Virtual Private Network) where you can enable the VPN in the settings to be on while using your mobile network, just adding that additional peace of mind for you. Do note that when using a VPN your data speeds will not be at their full potential, that being said I was very shocked to see that while using Google’s VPN I was still able to get speeds of 295Mbps on downloads, which is plenty fast for what I’m doing on my phone.

The camera on the Pixel 8 is the star of the phone and is nothing short of exceptional. Google’s expertise in computational photography paired with intuitive AI truly shines here. Meet the new boss, same as the old boss. GOOD
- Nice display with variable refresh rate
- Special AI features for camera
- No bloatware
- Great options for importing data from other phones

BAD
- Still no micro SD slot
- More expensive than last year

TLDR

The Pixel 8 is a little smaller than the Pixel 7, has a slightly better display and camera features, and costs $100 more.

DETAILS

The main benefit of the Pixel series of phones is what you don't get: bloatware and forced apps.  Most other manufacturers tend to stuff some extra apps on the phone, many of which you can't remove.  The Pixel thankfully doesn't do this.  It also uses a normal Android UI and not some weird in-house overlay or change to the navigation.

In comparison to the Pixel 7, the Pixel 8 doesn't change a whole lot.  The body is a little smaller at 6.2" instead of 6.3".  That makes it 5mm shorter and 3mm less side-to-side.  I like this change because I thought the Pixel 7 was always at the edge of being too big to use with one hand.  The corners are also a little more rounded than they were on the 7, something I don't like as much.  The display has the same 2400x1080 resolution, but it now supports a variable 60 - 120 Hz refresh rate instead of the fixed 90hz on the Pixel 7.  Most people probably won't notice the difference, honestly, though hopefully being able to use a slower refresh rate will help the battery go longer.

A lot of people had complaints about the Pixel 7 battery life, but I wasn't one of them.  I could easily get two, sometimes three days on a charge, and I can do the same with the 8.  However, I don't use my phone every waking second of the day either, so perhaps my experience doesn't apply to a lot of people.  Charging is still done over wired USB-C ( data connection, too ), and wireless charging is also still built-in.

Pixels also make it easy for people to transition from other phones.  If you're coming from a previous Pixel device, the two will automatically recognize each other when you power the new Pixel on and will ask to start the data transfer.  The Pixel also has the option to import data and settings from your old phone over a direct wired connection.  In the box is a USB-A to C adapter.  You connect your old phone to its data cable, use the A-to-C adapter on the other end of the cable, and plug that into the Pixel.  This even works with iPhones.  While this grabs your contacts, calendars, mail accounts, Wi-Fi settings, and other things, it still doesn't import all system configuration settings.  Even importing from a Pixel 7, I still had to go through system settings to change my display text size or reconfigure some apps.

Google still refuses to put a micro SD slot on their phones.  I guess they're still trying to force everyone to use their online storage so they have complete control over your data, same as Apple does.

Also a bummer is the phone selling for $100 more than the Pixel 7 released at last year ( and still sells for ).  Being able to get a flagship phone like the 7 for $600 when so many others were $800 and up was a great deal.  Being $700 now is still less expensive than some alternatives, but it's certainly a damper on the value.

For someone already on a Pixel 7, the 8 is a minimal upgrade and probably one you don't need, especially after only a year of use.

Almost perfect. One big problem though.. I came from a Pixel 7 Pro. Below are my thoughts:

Pros:

- Amazing battery. Moto, keep up whatever you do with the battery. I get more than double the battery life on this, than I did on my Pixel 7 Pro. Keep it up! The battery is the best I've used on any device. 

- The screen is beautiful. 

- Moto features are great. 

- Customization is great. much better than the pixel. 

- Software is stable. Very few bugs. I only encountered maybe 2 small bugs in the 3 months I've owned this. They were resolved by resetting app preferences. I forget the bugs frankly, they were so minor. It's a much more stable experience than I ever had with the Pixel devices. 

- Performance is very snappy. 

- The front camera is good quality (much better than pixel 7 pro). 

- Rear camera photos are pretty good, but not amazing.  (NOT INCLUDING TELEPHOTO. Telephoto is awful. see cons below on the telephoto ).  


Cons:

- Please add something for accidental touches on the side of the screen. I've had other curved screens but never had this issue where my pam would activate touches. 

- Please improve the swipe to split gesture. It's a great concept but I accidentally activate it all the time. 

- Security updates are very slow compared to competitors. If you want to do bi monthly security updates, fine, but please keep your word of bi monthly. And please make it that month's update. I received Nov 2023's security patch in the second week of December 2023. Why not just sent out the December patch? 

- Android system updates are very delayed which is disappointing. I heard last year's flagships didn't receive Android 13 until after Android 14 released. That's unacceptable. 

- The lack of premium cases and screen protectors is very annoying. Please partner with some companies to make these. Dbrand, Mous, etc. it took me 2 months to find a decent screen protector (look up Gadget Guard). I still haven't found a good premium case. 

- The telephoto camera is absolutely awful. This is the worst thing about this device. This phone might as well not even have it. It's a waste. The photos taken at 5x+ zoom aren't even worth taking. It's a blurry mess. In 2023/2024, this is unacceptable for a flagship device.

The telephoto camera quality is the worst thing about this device, hands down. 


**TLDR: Great overall phone. Amazing battery. Very stable device. Amazing performance. Poor software support schedule. Abysmal telephoto camera quality. 3/5**

Good. So I recently bought this phone as I have been a pixel user for over 5 years. Customer service was fantastic when I bought it at Best Buy, Nice, and everyone was friendly. So I am not going to blame the staff on this as they had no making on the phone. Google did however. 

I mainly just bought this as an upgrade to my 3a. But what I was mainly looking forward to was the camera quality. I saw many great reviews for the camera online and done and did as much research as I could. Animation is smooth, mic is nice and clear. Little to no background noise which is awesome. It's slick and an overall good phone. Now the reason I have 3 stars is because I believe it's over hyped and inconsistent. I compared the camera quality to my 3a and the front facing camera is more consistent in color, sharper, and adaptive, yes there is noise but compared to the 7 pro it honestly looks like the same amount of noise. The 7pro is smoother yes, but it's just a blurred mess. Colors aren't consistent and there was an automatic beauty filter applied??? That randomly turned off when I started comparing it to my 3a and how the front facing camera was more consistent and sharper. (I was talking out loud about my comparisons.) Front facing is just blurred out to make it look good for whoever takes selfies. And for the people thinking that MAYBE it might be the setting, no it wasn't. I put the same camera settings on both phones to compare the 2. I'm just disappointed honestly, my 5 year old phone has clearer camera quality on front camera than the 7 pro. I will also say the same about video. Which on both camera and video it's more tight as if it were already "pre-zoomed" in when it's not. My 3a gives a room and is consistent in distance. 

Now comparing it to the back camera, there we can see the camera upgrade and better quality. The 7pro is sharper, more adaptive, zoomed in all the way to 30x there's noise but that's kind of expected. If I were to compare it to Samsung it would be an unfair comparison. Now, if I were to compare it to the pixel a series I'd say that there is an obvious upgrade, especially with the ultrawide angle lense, zooming in, and the obvious changes compared to the a series. The phone is just average in my opinion, definitely in upgrade to the pixel 6 as well, but overall just average, in my opinion. 

Other things, phone gets hot fast, finger reader doesn't work as well, but google fixed that with screen protector mode (still kinda of wonky, but it helps), battery life is consistent, Google assistant doesn't pick up when whispering on 7pro, when compared to my 3a, it does. Display is beautiful to look at. Home screen gives minimal space to work with with widgets, but that's not really a big issue. Knowing these things I probably would have switched to Samsung just to give them a try. I still love Google and there pixel series, I just think it needs a bit more work. 

I hope this has been a good review for those seriously interested in purchasing the 7pro. Again, I don't blame best buy, they're just the messenger, but I do blame it on Google. It's a good phone, I'm just calling out the things I've noticed.

The cameras are all the same from the 8 pro models, but they are up to speed with other competitors in the market.   But I do wish they were improved more for the upgraded price of the new pixel line up.    However, I would recommend the phone for anyone needing a new phone or upgrade.

Goodbye Samsung, Again!. I decided to give Samsung another chance after the S24 Ultra disappointed me, hoping the S25 Ultra would finally change my mind. I even got the 512GB at a great deal at $1099 and really wanted to keep it. But after 2 weeks eventually I had to return it. And honestly? I felt such a huge wave of relief once I did.

The experience was inconsistent, especially when it came to the battery life. Even after I followed all the battery guidelines and turned off things in the settings, the battery would still drain unnaturally fast even with light use. It gave me constant anxiety. With iPhones, the battery just lasts and lets me forget it.

As for the apps and UI, it’s true what many have said: Samsung’s software just doesn’t match the polish of iOS. It felt fragmented, clunky, and unrefined. Small things like app animations, message delivery delays, or inconsistent design choices constantly reminded me that I wasn’t on iOS. And while most people may not notice or care, to me, the user experience is everything.

The camera had its moments. But despite the hype around the 100x zoom, it was nearly useless in real-life scenarios like concerts or dim lighting, where the iPhone’s much lower zoom still produced clearer, more usable photos.

Still, Samsung has great things: best display, customization, and freedom of Android.

If you’re thinking of switching from iPhone, I really recommend giving it at least two full weeks.

Proof you don't need an expensive phone. I'm not a "rewarded review" and don't need to exaggerate.  For reference, my main phone now is a Pixel 6a but I'm really considering using this Samsung A15 5g as my new main phone.  I won't lie, there's two things that hold this phone back from being a 5 star review.  Those things are this only has one bottom single firing speaker and the RAM is less than I'd prefer.  I got a black Friday deal on this phone and have only used it for two days, but overall performance has been fantastic! Benchmark numbers for the Pixel 6a and my previous iPhone 13 were both higher but this A15 holds right up against them.  Whether I'm doing basics,gaming(light games are all I play), listening to music,or making/receiving phone calls, this phone handles it all with relative ease.  And rather fast too.  Many reviews here and elsewhere had me anxious about whether this phone could perform without serious lagging.  To my pleasant surprise, it keeps up with anything you want to do and aside from during setup, there hasn't been any real lags or slow down.  It won't perform like a $1,000 phone which is common sense but it will do everything an expensive phone does maybe just not as fast.  If this phone had dual speakers and just a tad more RAM, it'd be perfect.  On the RAM, use the device care cleaner and delete individual apps' cache often.  That'll ensure your phone runs like a champ like mine does.  Also, restarting your phone once a day or every few days will free up RAM to optimize it too. I use device care many times per day to release any memory that can be freed up. I'm surprised Android users don't already know these tips in 2024 but it'll make a huge performance difference.  Unless you're a high end phone snob or too lazy to do my tips, this phone is surprisingly great.

Maybe. First impressions:
The pink color is gorgeous in person — soft, modern, and not too flashy. It’s more of a subtle blush than a bright pink, which gives it a classy and fresh vibe. The size feels great in the hand if you’re used to bigger phones, and the aluminum edges make it feel sturdy but not too heavy.

 Screen & Design:
The 6.7-inch Super Retina XDR display is stunning — bright, sharp, and excellent for watching videos or browsing. The colors are vivid and text looks crisp. It’s flat (not curved), which I actually like because it feels more precise when tapping near the edges.

 Performance:
The A16 Bionic chip is super fast — apps open instantly, multitasking is smooth, and even games run like butter. You won’t feel like this phone is slowing down anytime soon. It’s basically as fast as the 14 Pro from last year, which is a win.

 Camera:
The 48MP main camera is a huge upgrade. Photos come out detailed, bright, and really natural-looking. The color balance is solid, and low-light performance is impressive for a non-Pro iPhone. The new 2x zoom mode gives a bit more flexibility, and selfies look sharp too.

 Battery life:
This is one of the best parts. The iPhone 15 Plus can easily last all day and into the next morning with moderate use. Streaming, texting, social media, and even some video recording — no problem.

 USB-C port:
Finally! Charging and data transfer now work with USB-C, which is more convenient if you have other modern devices. But you’ll need new cables if you’ve been using Lightning.

 Little things:
	•	Dynamic Island is a fun, interactive touch — not a game-changer, but a nice improvement.
	•	No 120Hz refresh rate (only 60Hz), which Pro models have — not a dealbreaker, but worth noting.
	•	No telephoto lens — just wide and ultra-wide.

⸻
 Pros:
	•	Beautiful, soft pink color
	•	Great battery life
	•	Strong performance
	•	Excellent main camera
	•	USB-C port (finally!)

Cons:
	•	Only 60Hz display (not as smooth as Pro models)
	•	No telephoto lens
	•	A bit large for small hands

⸻

 Final Thoughts:

If you want a big, beautiful iPhone with great battery life, a reliable camera, and a gorgeous pink color, the iPhone 15 Plus is a fantastic choice. It’s not a “Pro,” but it does almost everything most people need — and looks amazing while doing it.

From the perspective of an international student, finding a reliable and affordable phone that can handle daily needs is essential. The Samsung Galaxy A16 5G seems to be a solid choice that fits this description. One of its key strengths is its affordability and great value. Managing a student budget is crucial, and this phone delivers without being overly expensive. The ability to use it with different carriers, possibly with a dual-SIM feature, is also a huge advantage, allowing me to easily switch between local and international SIM cards. The large, bright AMOLED screen makes watching online lectures or streaming content a pleasant experience. Furthermore, the promise of up to six years of software updates is a major plus, ensuring the phone will remain secure and functional throughout my academic program. The decent battery life lasts through a full day of classes, and the primary camera is perfectly capable of taking clear photos of documents and for social media.
However, there are some downsides to consider. The processor, while adequate for basic tasks like web browsing and social media, can struggle with more demanding activities, leading to some lag when multitasking. The plastic build, while durable, doesn't feel as premium as some higher-end devices. Additionally, the absence of a charger in the box is a minor inconvenience, requiring a separate purchase. Finally, the secondary ultrawide camera isn't as high-quality as the main lens and can produce lower-quality.

Design & Display: 
Samsung’s design language continues to impress, and the S24 Ultra is no exception. The sleek, polished finish gives it a refined, premium feel that stands out in any crowd. The 6.8-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display is nothing short of spectacular. With vivid colors, perfect blacks, and a buttery-smooth 120Hz refresh rate, it’s a visual treat for gaming, video streaming, and general use. Brightness levels are superb, even in direct sunlight, making it a joy to use indoors or out.

Camera:
The camera setup on the Galaxy S24 Ultra is exceptional, featuring a 200MP primary sensor that captures incredibly sharp, detailed images in a variety of lighting conditions. The 12MP ultra-wide camera and two telephoto lenses (3x and 10x optical zoom) offer incredible versatility for all types of photography. Low-light performance is excellent, and the AI-based software ensures your shots are optimized automatically. Video recording is just as impressive, with smooth stabilization and rich color reproduction.

Battery
With a 5,000mAh battery, the S24 Ultra comfortably lasts through a full day of moderate to heavy usage. Whether you're browsing, streaming, or gaming, it won’t let you down. The 45W fast charging support means you can charge up quickly when you need to, and wireless charging is supported as well. The only small downside is that the fast-charging speeds aren't the absolute fastest compared to some other devices, but it’s still more than sufficient for daily use.

Having used Pixel 7, I can tell this is the best Google phone so far, with most of the quirks of previous Pixels fixed in this iteration, including infuriating fingerprint sensors, heating issues, network/signal issues, and somehow unpleasant pictures (maybe mine was a lemon camera setup on the 7; compared to my S22 and S23+ ) on the Pixel 7.

I was stuck with a few months old fully paid S23+ and was looking to get rid for a meager few hundred bucks and then this phone deal showed up. I immediately grabbed the deal,  and on release day, traded in my S23+ at a local bestbuy along with a free $200 gift card, which made the Pixel 9 Pro XL completely free, and also made some profit with the gift card. 

I'm loving this phone and really glad I was able to score one. With all major previous Pixel issues fixed, this phone feels phenomenal; really high quality, flagship level, with the looks of the top of the line iPhone, and the best part is the gigantic 16 GB RAM (plus free 1 year of Gemini advanced, if you care). Fingerprint scanner works flawlessly, and is really quick; doesn't heat up; cameras are almost awesome, giving out great pictures. Videos and CPU may not be as great as Apple's, but still more than sufficient for almost everyone; you'll hardly feel any difference when it comes to performance.

Only gripe is the terribly slow auto-focus with close-up shots, specially when scanning bar codes. For instance, when scanning bar codes of a driver license/id, you'd need luck for it to actually scan fast. My more than 5 different id/license barcode scans usually took multiple attempts for a successful scan, and sometimes taking upto a minute or longer also, and you'd actually have to try bringing the id closer and farther away for focus to work, which sucks if you have to do this as part of your job. My previous S22 and S23+ worked flawlessly when scanning barcodes, with fast close-up autofocus.

If you don't care for barcode scans, then this phone is definitely one of the best, and I highly recommend this phone, maybe not for the full price, but when great deals pop up, try grabbing one.

Pleasantly Surprised. As the title says, I was pleasantly surprised by this phone. In the past two weeks of using it, I have found that the Google assistant was incredibly helpful in more ways than one, and having the always on  display was a nice bonus. 

Positives:
- It is a great size, and has a good balanced weight
- The 90Hz OLED screen gets perfectly bright to see outdoors even in broad daylight
- Having WiFi 6E is a plus for future proofing
- Android 13 on a Pixel is the best way to experience it without any bloatware
- The cameras take amazing photos! Being able to do images like Photo Sphere as well as use Google's image editing tools such as the new Deblur / remove people is awesome!
- Reverse wireless charging for other wireless charging devices
- USB-C charging is quick at around 20W max
- Battery life is good and lasts all day (even more depending on usage)
- The fingerprint reader is quick, and the face unlock works fast in "good" lighting conditions.

Cons
- Wirelessly charging this device is very slow. While I have not tested with a Pixel Stand, using other 15W Qi charging pads this phone will not go above 5W. 


All in all, I was, as I said, pleasantly surprised by this phone. Flagship specs along with the incredible power of Google in both the Assistant being helpful in daily tasks to finding answers to questions such as air quality, weather, directions, etc., all using your voice is so great. Add in the fact that the OS is entirely Google means that the experience is generally cohesive and uniform across the Google apps. A home run!

I ordered the Straight Talk phone online and it was delivered from the store next day. I attempted to activate it and the CSR told me it hadn't been scanned so they couldn't activate it. I've bought a number of phones from Walmart and this was the first that wouldn't activate.  I returned it to the store today, was refunded, and bought another. It was scanned and I activated it this afternoon. I had the CSR rebrand it from Straight Talk to TracFone on activation. Verizon bought TracFone and owns all of their brands. The website listing says that the Moto g 5G has 64gb ROM, but the box and the phone says in settings that it has 4gb RAM and 128gb ROM. It also has RAM Boost, which is an optional feature that can add up to 4gb to RAM to double it to 8gb using the phone's internal memory, but it can be switched off. The phone has dual SIM, one a physical SIM card (pSIM) and a secondary eSIM slot. The phone has NFC, most lower priced Motos don't seem to have that these days. I also bought the AT%26T version of this phone and activated it on H20 Wireless. Overall it is a nicely performing phone for the price range. A person should look up its specs with a Google Search and perhaps watch some YouTube videos to decide if it's right for their needs. I do recommend that they buy phones in store instead of online if at all possible and supervise the barcode scan process if they're afraid their phone won't be scanned properly for activation. If buying at the store is a problem because it's too far away, the alternative is to order directly from the service provider. Throughout the process of returning and buying another phone, the store assistants were very considerate and helpful. Thank you.

First off, despite the many many news outlets describing the S25 Ultra as a minor incremental upgrade from even the S23 Ultra, that has been far from my experience.

My initial impression was that the flat screen and back are a nice change. This phone is much easier to hold, maintains the same screen size in a smaller package, and is now very easy to put a screen protector on.

Functionally speaking, battery life is much improved from my old S23 Ultra despite maintaining the same usage patterns and app load, and I find that the Galaxy AI features are nice - albeit a little underdeveloped at the moment.

Now Brief is a nice touch to the lock screen, and I placed a widget on my home screen as well. I am not seeing the full functionality of it at this time, despite having all content toggles flipped on (minus YouTube shorts.) I imagine this will be improved over time.

Regarding the Qi2 Ready moniker, I feel like this was so much more convoluted than it needed to be. Couple that with reports that Samsung didn't actually send technical specs for the phone for case makers to align the case-integrated magnet array, and you have a recipe for even more confusion. I haven't seen an increase in speed over my old wireless charger, which was not Qi2 and did not have magnetic alignment, despite buying Qi2 certified charger docks and adapters (both 120VAC and 12VDC.) Hopefully this is an issue that gets resolved in the future, but really, include the magnets in the phone next time!

This phone should be The Phone of the Year!. So I've been using the Google Pixel 9 Pro XL for about 6 days now and I've got to say that for the first time in a long time.. I'm excited to step out and use my new phone. I'll start by saying that I consider myself a photographer and videographer. I'm not a pro by any means but I enjoy sharing photos and videos of life and the world around me. If you are reading this review.. odds are by now you already know that the Google Pixel line of phones are known to have some of the best camera hardware and software in a smartphone. This year's Google Pixel has a 42mp front facing camera, a 48 mp ultra wide camera, a 48 mp telephoto camera that Zooms up to 30X ! and a 50mp wide camera. It's loaded! 
I've had so much fun going out for walks and capturing photos and videos with this phone. It is jam packed with so many fun camera features and editing tricks. I've tried a lot of them and I'm still finding new things to do with it each time I dig through the menus. You can toggle between a 12mp and 50mp setting but oddly enough I've found that leaving it set to 12mp seems to create sharper photos. If you select 50 mp setting and zoom in past 5x the photos tend to look super soft and mushy. Don't know if it's just the way it is, or if it'll need to be fixed with a future software update. Anywhooo. if you leave it at the default setting, you will be super pleased with photos taken with each lens on this phone. The Google camera app makes taking creative photos and videos so easy. My favorite modes so far have been "action pan", "add me" , and video "Pan". There is a bunch of other cool photo and video modes to play with as well. "Add me" allows you take a group photo of your friends and loved ones, then you hand the phone to someone in the group while you step into the shot and have them take a photo with you in it. The software will add you into the previous photo and everyone will be in the photo! 
This year's Google pixel has an excellent video camera. I feel like google phones in the past always had mediocre video quality, but this time around it has really impressed me! I can't wait to take it to a concert or other event and capture some cool videos! The camera app also has a mode called "video boost" when recording. You have to toggle it on every time you are about to record a video but it will upload the video to Google's servers, process it and hand it back to you with better dynamic range, contrast and even render unto 8k 30 FPS if you would like! Oh man, I'm sorry but I could talk about the cameras all day long. If you've made it this far.. just take my word for it, you will love the cameras on this phone. 

The rest of the specs on this phone are pretty great, you get the new Google Tensor G4 chip, and Gemini Nano / Titan M2 chip. It has 16 gb of ram, and this variant has 128GB of storage. Not enough if you ask me. Especially if you are like me and love taking photos and videos. You will have to offload photos and videos onto a hard drive or the cloud often. The phone supports 5G, wifi 7, bluetooth 5.3 and has an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor under the screen. The fingerprint sensor is very fast and reliable. I have not had any issues unlocking my phone. The screen is 6.8 inches and very bright! Google claims 3000 nits, but I leave adaptive brightness on so it doesn't hit its peak brightness often unless I am outside. it is very usable outdoors in this bright Texas sun. 

The hardware specs on this phone won't be the best on the market, but where this phone shines is the software included on here. There is a ton of Google Ai software in here. So much that I still have yet to use every feature fully. Google introduced "Gemini" on this Pixel. I believe it is the name of the new artificial intelligence program that I'm guessing will replace Google Assistant in the future. I wasn't able to try the "gemini advanced" mode because it is subscription based model and it seems to conflict with the Google One plan I already have. So I can't speak of all the features that Gemini Advanced will provide but from what I've used so far.. I would say that it's been pretty useful for day to day tasks. I still feel kind of weird letting Ai do my work or thinking for me, but I suppose as time goes on I will get used to it. One of my favorite features so far is "call notes". When you call someone or a business.. the phone call will be recorded and then transcribed or summarized for you with notes. I know I know.. low key creepy. But I can see it being helpful. Especially when calling to make an appointment or if someone provides you a phone number or other information that needs to be written down. If you decide to use the call notes feature, it will play a message in the call saying that the call is being recorded so that the person on the other line is made aware of it. 
There is so many helpful and cool software tricks on this phone that I am going to suggest that you go online and read all about them. The phone will also have plenty of helpful tips and guides to walk you through them all. If I haven't lost your attention yet, I feel like I will if I keep on going on about all the software features on this phone lol. But I will say.. there is so much helpful smart software packed into this phone that you'll be learning about it all for weeks. 

The build quality of this phone is very nice. I love it actually. It is lightweight but solid. The back of the phone has a nice soft texture to the touch. the glass on the back does not get greasy or slippery. The rails are polished aluminum and look very beautiful. The camera is raised looks pretty futuristic lol, but it will not make the phone rock when laid on its back. I love this phone, I want to carry it without a case.. but for now.. I Don't want to risk breaking it. Google says the phone is 2x more durable than last years! How durable exactly? I don't know, but glass can break, and polish aluminum can scratch.. so I'll keep it in a case for a while. 

I know, this review is quite long, and I'm sure I missed a lot. But the TLDR is 
This is the first Google phone I have been excited for in a long time. It's also the first phone I've enjoyed taking photos and videos with as much as I enjoy shooting with mirrorless cameras. 
My only complaint is that 128gb is not enough for this phone. You will definitely need to rely on a cloud service, most likely Google's cloud services.. and or a hard drive to store all your recorded memories. 
Google says it will provide 7 years of updates to this phone, you will definitely fill the storage on this phone very quickly. If you are like me and already subscribe to Google One or some other cloud storage, then you will be fine with this bare minimum. If you don't want to pay a subscription for cloud storage, then I suggest you but a variant with more storage. 

Would I recommend this phone? 100% for sure. Especially if you are already a fan of android phones, and or Google phones. If you've been waiting for a phone to make the switch from the fruit company, I think you will also love this phone. The cameras and the magic editor software alone are the best reason to make that switch

Worth Serious Consideration. So, I am coming over to Pixel from another brand. The experience has been interesting
as I have never had a Pixel Phone before, However, I have always had Android phones
for the most part. This will be my comparison and experience.

First impression out of the box feels like a solid build and maybe a little weightier 
than my current phone. The glass back somehow resists fingerprints. 
Initial set up went smooth cloning my old phone to the Pixel via USB C cable.
There was some updating and I was off and running. Had to learn how to use this 
Phone but I will address that later. 

The first glitch I ran into was watching a YouTube music video. The volume was
Very weak. I found the bottom speaker had no volume at all and the top earpiece 
speaker barely had volume. I decided to check for more updates and thus, a 
security update was available. Proceeded to install and checked after a few hours and
phone was still installing. Left on over night and found installed next morning so I
rebooted the phone and checked all features again and found I now had full volume
out of both speakers. The sound is now actually pretty good and nice loud volume.
The low end and midrange frequencies are lacking. High end treble appears to be 
The norm for this phone but satisfied with the volume output which is quite good. 

Now going through a pure android experience vs a 4.1 UI from another brand was 
slightly disappointing. I am still researching this to see if there is any tweaking
whatsoever that I am missing.
My other phone’s UI allowed me to customize folders and apps with color schemes. 
All folder and app drawers for the Pixel are one color. Nothing exciting.
I barely use the Gmail app due to the amount of emails I receive at times. Gmail 
will not allow you delete all at once and that to me is a time waster. 
Do not disturb turned on allowed me to be disturbed. I figured out which app was being 
Naughty and tried to disable some of the apps features (button in app was blue
Indicating it was turned on) I could not turn it off. Only choice was to force stop. 
Now I do realize this could be a compatibility issue with the app and android 13,
Not necessarily the Pixels’ fault. 

The Good Stuff:
Camera is amazing, especially being a non pro phone version. Really liked that 
I could erase objects or people in the pictures without any noticeable changes.
Clarity of the camera is very good. I did have bit of a learning curve at first.
The screen does get very bright which I like in a phone. 
I am enjoying the 5G UC connection with TMobile that this phone is utilizing.
Blazing Fast connection!! See Pic. Speed test may vary depending on where 
your at and interference. 
I thought I might be disappointed going to a slightly smaller 6.3” phone from
6.7” plus phone but I actually like the smaller form factor in my pocket and
difference in size is minimal. 

I am finding android 13 is very fluid and smooth and worth the experience.
I am finding once the phone learns your preferences it pretty much is fast
at executing the commands.
For me, one of the most noticeable features is the voice recognition. So 
far I have not had any strange words or sentences when using voice 
recognition dictation. I was constantly making corrections with my 
previous phone which again is a time waster. 
Unless you really need the pro version, The 7 will be more than adequate 
For most users.

In summary, the Pixel 7 is a solid choice for anyone invested in the Android ecosystem. It offers an excellent camera, robust performance, and a clean, user-friendly OS. Great phone but not without its issues.. Even though I was very happy with my Razr 5G I recently decided to try out the new Razr Plus. The major selling points for me personally were the larger inner and outer displays, improved camera functions, and the fact that the flip can now stay halfway open which eliminates the need for a tripod when taking photos and videos. I just don’t like to take hand held selfies as the camera really needs to be farther than arms length away in order to avoid the distortion of features. Also when I had to take new passport photos a few years ago it was a real pain getting my old Razr proped up in the right position without a tripod and then setting the timer before quickly getting into position. With the new Razr however I can easily get it pointing where I want and then just by holding up my hand in front of the camera a 3-second countdown timer will automatically start. Its also great not having to hold the phone while on video calls as you can just set it on the table rather than holding it in front of your face the whole time. I also like the fact that the fingerprint reader on this phone is much easier to use than on the previous model. As for the larger outer display its really fantastic and very functional but for some reason I still find myself habitually opening the phone up to do things that could now easily be done on the outer display. It’s just hard to break old habits I guess. 

Anyway, even though I am very happy with the new phone overall there are a few problems worth mentioning. First of all, unlike the previous model, the Razr Plus comes with a factory installed screen protector for some reason and after only four months of use it has starting to crease and crack at the fold. The phone will also no longer quite open a full 180 degrees and I suspect that this is also due to the damaged screen protector. I obviously need to have it replaced as soon as possible as any sharp edges from the crack could potentially damage the screen underneath. However since simply removing it oneself will void the warranty I must take it in and have it done at a Motorola partner service center – something which is easier said than done apparently. After calling Motorola they were supposed to make an appointment for me at a service center near me but he was unable to make the appointment online for some reason and so he gave me the phone number instead. Then after I was unable to get through by phone I drove out to the place only to learn that they do not have the screen protectors for this phone and they cannot even get them. It looks like my only choice now may be to send it in to Motorola and I really don’t want to have to do this every 3 or 4 months. I’m seriously considering just peeling off the screen protector myself and hoping I don’t need any warranty service over the next 8 months. My last Razr did not even have a screen protector and that display still looks and works great. Although ironically if a screen protector had come on the previous generation, it probably would not have cracked as the diameter of the fold in the display is much larger on the previous generation. This by the way is the main reason I chose the Razr 5G over the Samsung back then in the first place. I could just tell by examining the two that the Samsung screen would be much more likely to crack over time – as they indeed did. But now the new Razr Plus has a screen fold that is closer to the Samsung than to the previous Razr, 

Another downside of the new phone is that the flip is much harder to open one handed. With my Razr 5G it was very easy to open it one handed with a flick of the wrist. But it takes so much force to do this with the new model that I’m afraid the hinge could sustain damage. Also, having to flick with that much force makes it more likely that it could fly out of your hand and get damaged.  Of course this cant really be helped and it is simply the price we must pay for having a flip that can stay half open at 90-degrees. Anyway, I have basically just resigned myself to always having to open it with both hands. As for the hinge itself it seems fairly sturdy but still not quite as sturdy as on the previous generation in my opinion.

Another big downside for me is the fact that on the Razer plus you are no longer able to plug wired headphones in by using the USB-C adapter. I just like having the option of using a wired connection when need be. For example, when the battery is dead on my Bluetooth headset or when I want to listen to music on my home stereo system which does not have Bluetooth. Its just really stupid that they disabled this function in the new Razr Plus. 

Still, other than these issues it's a great little foldable.
